The evidence here is unusually strong for a causal claim in a rare disease, because it is a reversibility experiment: microliths transferred into wild-type mouse lungs produce inflammation that peaks at one week and resolves at one month as the stones are cleared. That the inflammation goes away with the stones is what makes stone burden a target rather than a bystander.

evidence.snippet: While it remains static in some patients, it progresses into pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory failure and cor pulmonale in others.
evidence.explanation: States the fibrotic progression and its endpoints, and simultaneously records that the course bifurcates rather than progressing uniformly.

steps/7.description: Progressive interstitial fibrosis with restrictive ventilatory defect and falling diffusion capacity. This is the arm that conforms to the conserved fibrotic response, with alveolar epithelial injury and stone-driven inflammation as the disease-specific upstream trigger.

evidence.snippet: Many patients are asymptomatic and the majority of patients either have normal or restrictive pulmonary function.
evidence.explanation: Records restriction as the abnormal pattern when there is one, and simultaneously that normal physiology is common.

steps/8.description: Restriction on pulmonary function testing as fibrosis advances. Notably, many patients have entirely normal physiology despite a florid radiograph, which is part of the same radiographic-clinical dissociation that characterises the disease.

evidence.snippet: While it remains static in some patients, it progresses into pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory failure and cor pulmonale in others.
evidence.explanation: Names cor pulmonale as an endpoint of the progressive course.

steps/9.description: Right heart failure secondary to advanced parenchymal lung disease, and part of the terminal picture. The associated pulmonary hypertension here is secondary to lung disease and hypoxia rather than a primary pulmonary arteriopathy, which is why this phenotype is bound to cor pulmonale rather than to a pulmonary arterial hypertension term.

evidence.snippet: While it remains static in some patients, it progresses into pulmonary fibrosis, respiratory failure and cor pulmonale in others.
evidence.explanation: Names respiratory failure as an endpoint of the progressive course.

steps/10.description: The usual cause of death in progressive disease, and the indication for transplantation.

edges/1.description: Loss of the transporter, or of its transport activity, removes the only significant route by which phosphate leaves the alveolar space.

edges/2.description: Phosphate liberated by surfactant phospholipid breakdown has nowhere to go.

edges/3.description: Precipitated calcium phosphate organises into discrete concretions.

edges/4.description: Demonstrated by adoptive transfer rather than inferred: stones placed in a normal lung provoke inflammation, and the inflammation resolves as they are cleared.

edges/5.description: Surfactant accumulation was an unexpected finding in the mouse model. It closes a loop back to the surfactant biology that supplies the phosphate in the first place, but the intermediates between stone burden and phospholipidosis are not established.

edges/6.description: Reached through the inflammatory response to the stones rather than by direct mechanical injury.

edges/7.description: Chronic macrophage-driven inflammation drives the fibrotic remodelling that produces restriction.

edges/8.description: Fibrosis stiffens the lung and reduces volumes.

edges/9.description: Reached through hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction and vascular remodelling secondary to the parenchymal disease, rather than through a primary pulmonary arteriopathy.

edges/10.description: The terminal common pathway and the usual cause of death.

evidence.snippet: From this region, we have identified a gene that has mutations in all patients with pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis.
evidence.explanation: The second independent 2006 identification of the gene, quoted at its actual finding rather than at its title: a positional search that recovered mutations in every patient studied.

genes/0.notes: Encodes NaPi-IIb, the type IIb sodium-dependent phosphate cotransporter. Biallelic loss-of-function variants cause the disease, and were identified independently by two groups in 2006. Loss of transport does not require loss of protein: some variants reach the membrane but cannot move phosphate, which the 2026 cryo-EM structures rationalise by showing that transport depends on sodium-driven conformational transitions rather than on the transporter merely being present. Sibling transporters SLC34A1 and SLC34A3 cause renal phosphate-wasting disease, so the same protein family produces very different disease depending on which epithelium expresses it.

evidence.snippet: There is currently no cure for PAM, and the only effective treatment is lung transplantation
evidence.explanation: States plainly that transplantation is the only effective treatment, which is the claim this record carries.

treatments/0.description: The only effective treatment, and the only one that alters outcome. Both single and bilateral procedures are performed for end-stage disease. Microliths have not been documented to recur in transplanted lungs, which is not merely a good outcome but a mechanistic result: it indicates the defect is intrinsic to the lung epithelium rather than a systemic disorder of mineral handling that would recalcify any lung installed.

evidence.snippet: Eighteen months postoperatively, he continues to do well with normalized pulmonary and cardiac function
evidence.explanation: Documents normalisation of both pulmonary and cardiac function after transplantation in a patient with severe pre-operative pulmonary hypertension.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Replaces the epithelium that carries the transporter defect, restoring normal alveolar phosphate handling in the graft. This is why the treatment is curative for the lung rather than palliative, and why non-recurrence in grafts is the expected result rather than a lucky one.

evidence.snippet: Patients with PAM should be offered preventative and symptomatic treatments such as vaccinations and oxygen therapy when needed.
evidence.explanation: Names the components of supportive management recommended for this disease.

evidence.snippet: PAM management is basically supportive using vaccines, antibiotics in recurrent infections, or long-term oxygen when respiratory failure is determined.
evidence.explanation: Independent statement of the same supportive components, including antibiotics for recurrent infection.

treatments/1.description: What most patients actually receive: vaccination against respiratory pathogens, antibiotics for intercurrent infection, and long-term oxygen once respiratory failure develops. None of it modifies the underlying process.

evidence.snippet: there are no proven treatments for PAM
evidence.explanation: Refutes a claim of proven pharmacological benefit for any agent in this disease. Recorded as REFUTE rather than omitted so that a reader learns the obvious candidates have been tried, not that nobody thought of them.

treatments/2.description: Bisphosphonate therapy tried on the reasoning that a drug inhibiting mineral deposition in bone might inhibit it in lung. The result is the most interesting negative in the disease: radiographic improvement has been reported in some children over sustained treatment, but the response varies even between family members carrying identical variants, and benefit in adults is limited.

evidence.snippet: there are no proven treatments for PAM
evidence.explanation: Refutes proven benefit for this procedure along with every other non-transplant option. Curated as its own record rather than bundled, because the reason saline lavage fails here is specific to the physical form of the deposits and is worth stating.

treatments/3.description: Therapeutic lavage, borrowed from the management of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis where it is genuinely effective. It does not work here, and the reason is instructive rather than incidental: proteinosis fills the alveoli with material that can be washed out, whereas the stones of this disease are frequently larger than the airway lumen and simply will not come. Recovering some microliths in the effluent is not the same as clearing the burden.

evidence.snippet: Microliths isolated by bronchoalveolar lavage readily dissolve in EDTA, and therapeutic whole-lung EDTA lavage reduces the burden of stones in the lungs.
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL because the result is entirely murine. No human has been treated this way, and whole-lung lavage with a chelating agent would require its own safety case before that could change.

treatments/4.description: The mechanistically motivated successor to saline lavage: rather than trying to rinse the stones out, dissolve them. Microliths recovered by lavage dissolve readily in EDTA, and therapeutic EDTA lavage reduces stone burden in the mouse. This is the difference between rinsing gravel and dissolving it, and it has not been tried in humans.

evidence.snippet: Microliths isolated by bronchoalveolar lavage readily dissolve in EDTA, and therapeutic whole-lung EDTA lavage reduces the burden of stones in the lungs.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates both that the stones are chemically dissolvable and that lavage with a chelator reduces burden in vivo.

treatments/4/targets/0.description: Acts on the accumulated stones themselves by chelating the calcium that holds them together, reducing burden rather than preventing formation.

evidence.snippet: A low-phosphate diet prevents microlith formation in young animals and reduces lung injury on the basis of reduction in serum SP-D.
evidence.explanation: PARTIAL because the demonstration is murine and prevention in young animals is a different claim from benefit in an adult patient who already has a lung full of stones. Reported human dietary restriction lowered serum phosphate without halting progression.

treatments/5.description: Restricting dietary phosphate attacks the supply side of the mechanism. In the mouse it both prevents microlith formation in young animals and diminishes established deposits within four weeks, which is the only evidence anywhere that the burden of existing stones can be reduced by anything other than removing the lung. Human dietary restriction has been attempted and lowered serum phosphate without arresting the disease, so the murine result should not be read as translated.

evidence.snippet: A low-phosphate diet prevents microlith formation in young animals and reduces lung injury on the basis of reduction in serum SP-D.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates prevention in young animals with a biomarker correlate of reduced lung injury.

treatments/5/targets/0.description: Reduces the phosphate available to supersaturate the alveolar lining fluid, acting upstream of nucleation rather than on stones already formed.

treatments/6.description: Autosomal recessive recurrence risk and cascade testing of siblings, who are frequently affected and often asymptomatic at the point the proband is diagnosed.

open_questions/0.rationale: Two independent observations point at the same missing factor. Etidronate has been reported to produce radiographic improvement in some patients while relatives with the same variant do not respond, and the natural history bifurcates, remaining static in some patients while progressing to fibrosis and respiratory failure in others. Identical genotypes with divergent outcomes is a statement about modifiers rather than about the primary defect, and nothing is currently known about what they are. Until that is understood, prognosis cannot be given from genotype and drug response cannot be predicted.

open_questions/1.rationale: The theoretical case is strong on every axis that usually matters. The disease is monogenic and recessive, so restoring function rather than silencing a dominant product is sufficient; the target cell is a single, defined population; the organ is directly accessible to inhaled delivery; the mouse indicates the phenotype is at least partly reversible when stone burden falls; and the disease progresses slowly enough to leave a wide therapeutic window. Despite this, no gene therapy, gene editing, or RNA therapeutic programme exists, and no interventional clinical trial has ever been registered with this disease as its condition. The gap is one of attention rather than of biology, and is recorded here because that is itself worth knowing.

evidence.snippet: The present report documents that lead-induced deficiency when sufficiently severe gives rise to findings similar to the hereditary disorder.
evidence.explanation: The phenocopy claim itself, stated by the same group that described the inherited disease.

evidence.snippet: It is found on chromosome 7, consists of 10 exons with alternative splicing of exon 2, and produces proteins 286 and 297 amino acids long.
evidence.explanation: The gene structure this node describes, from the paper that identified it.

evidence.snippet: Three homozygous mutations were identified in this gene in 4 subjects with P5'N-1 deficiency: codon 98 GAT-->GTT, Asp-->Val (linked to a silent polymorphism codon 92, TAC-->TAT), codon 177, CAA-->TAA, Gln-->termination, and IVS9-1, G-->T.
evidence.explanation: The first three disease alleles, showing the missense, nonsense and splice classes this node covers.

steps/2.description: Missense, nonsense, splice-site and in-frame deletion variants on both NT5C3A alleles. The gene sits on chromosome 7, has 10 exons with alternative splicing of exon 2, and encodes proteins of 286 and 297 amino acids. Molecular diagnosis was delayed by nearly three decades after the clinical description, partly because P5N pseudogenes on chromosomes 4 and 7 complicate the sequencing.

evidence.snippet: The nucleotidase activity in deficient red cells assayed less than 14%, and usually less than 10%, of normal and much less in terms of reticulocyte-rich blood, where it was consistently found to be increased.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the residual activity and makes the reticulocyte correction that this node depends on.

evidence.snippet: Western blot showed no sign of the presence of 5'-nucleotidase protein in the erythrocytes of both studied patients.
evidence.explanation: A case in which the loss is of the protein itself rather than of its catalytic activity.

steps/3.description: Enzyme activity in affected red cells falls to under 14 percent, usually under 10 percent, of normal. The deficit is larger than it looks on a raw assay: the enzyme is normally enriched in reticulocytes, so a reticulocyte-rich hemolytic sample should read high, and reading low against that expectation means the true deficit is greater than the ratio to normal whole blood suggests. In one severe case Western blot showed no detectable protein at all.

evidence.snippet: Total nucleotides in patient cells were present in amounts 3-6 times greater than normal, and approximately 80% contained pyrimidine.
evidence.explanation: The magnitude and the compositional shift this node asserts.

evidence.snippet: Patient erythrocytes uniquely contained large amounts of pyrimidine 5'-ribonucleotides.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the accumulating species as pyrimidine ribonucleotides specifically.

steps/4.description: Pyrimidine nucleotides released by ribosomal RNA breakdown during reticulocyte maturation carry a phosphate and cannot cross the membrane. Undephosphorylated, they are trapped. Total nucleotide rises three- to six-fold and roughly 80 percent of the pool becomes pyrimidine, against 97 percent or more adenine in a normal red cell - a compositional inversion, not merely an excess.

evidence.snippet: It is postulated that the prominent basophilic stippling results from retarded ribosomal RNA degradation secondary to accumulation of degradation products, namely pyrimidine 5'-ribonucleotides.
evidence.explanation: The proposed link from nucleotide accumulation to stippling, quoted with the authors' own "It is postulated" so the epistemic status is visible.

steps/5.description: The accumulated pyrimidine ribonucleotides feed back on the dismantling of ribosomal RNA, so undegraded rRNA persists in the maturing cell. This is the step the original authors proposed to connect the biochemical lesion to the morphological one, and it remains the standard account. The mechanism by which the cell is then destroyed is not equally well established.

evidence.snippet: Pyrimidine 5' nucleotidase (P5'N-1) deficiency is an autosomal recessive condition causing hemolytic anemia characterized by marked basophilic stippling and the accumulation of high concentrations of pyrimidine nucleotides within the erythrocyte.
evidence.explanation: Names the stippling as the characterising feature alongside the nucleotide accumulation that causes it.

steps/6.description: Aggregated undegraded ribosomal RNA visible on a Romanowsky-stained film as coarse blue granules throughout the erythrocyte. It is the diagnostic hallmark of the disease and, together with a nonspherocytic hemolytic picture and normal G6PD and pyruvate kinase, is what prompts the enzyme assay or the NT5C3A sequencing.

evidence.snippet: cN-III was first linked to a genetic defect , hereditary pyrimidine nucleotidase deficiency, associated to a nonspherocyt ic hemolytic anemia disorder of still unclear mechanism but metabolically characterized by abnormally high levels of pyrimidine compounds and ribonucleoproteins in erythrocytes, as evidenced by occurrence of basophilic stippling on blood smearings.
evidence.explanation: A review stating that the hemolytic mechanism remains unclear even though the metabolic lesion is well characterised. Quoted verbatim including the source's own typesetting artefacts.

evidence.snippet: No correlation has been found between residual activity and degree of hemolysis.
evidence.explanation: The dissociation between how much enzyme activity remains and how much hemolysis results. This is the strongest single reason this node is recorded as HYPOTHETICAL: if the amount of enzyme lost does not predict the amount of destruction, the step between them is not a simple dose-response and is not understood.

evidence.snippet: The mechanism responsible for increased red cell GSH is unknown.
evidence.explanation: The unexplained glutathione finding that has accompanied the disease since its description and is part of why the hemolytic step is unresolved.

evidence.snippet: In view of the increasing evidence that the hemolysis associated with pyrimidine 5' nucleotidase deficiency results not only from an increase in the level of erythrocyte pyrimidines, but also from inhibition of the hexose monophosphate shunt activity in young erythrocytes, it is likely that the marked instability of Hb E in the enzyme-deficient cells results from oxidant damage acting on a mildly unstable Hb variant.
evidence.explanation: Names the hexose-monophosphate-shunt candidate for the hemolytic step. Recorded as INDIRECT because the observation is about Hb E instability in deficient cells rather than about hemolysis in the isolated disorder, and quoted with the source's own "increasing evidence" and "it is likely".

steps/7.description:
Chronic extravascular hemolysis, ranging from fully compensated to transfusion-requiring. The step from the loaded, stippled cell to its premature clearance is the least well understood part of the chain: reviews describe the hemolytic mechanism as still unclear, and the raised reduced glutathione seen in patient cells has never been explained. The entry therefore records this edge as indirect with unknown intermediates rather than asserting a mechanism.
One candidate has real support and is worth naming rather than leaving out. Beyond the nucleotide load itself, inhibition of hexose monophosphate shunt activity in young erythrocytes has been proposed as a second contributor, which would make the cells oxidant-vulnerable. The evidence for it is indirect and comes from a co-inheritance experiment: in a family segregating both this deficiency and hemoglobin E, the doubly homozygous individual had severe hemolysis while each single homozygote was mild or asymptomatic, and globin-chain work traced that to marked instability of Hb E specifically in enzyme-deficient cells, with free alpha-chains accumulating on the membrane. Note the tension with the raised glutathione: an oxidative account has to accommodate a finding that points the other way, and no cited source reconciles them.

evidence.snippet: Among intrinsic causes of hemolysis, pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase (P5N) deficiency is a notable condition, often presenting as nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia.
evidence.explanation: Names the hemolytic picture that defines the clinical presentation.

steps/8.description: Chronic hemolysis without spherocytes, with normal osmotic fragility and normal G6PD and pyruvate kinase activity. Severity ranges from a compensated picture found incidentally to persistent transfusion-requiring crises.

evidence.snippet: The syndrome was characterized by marked increases above normal in red cell basophilic stippling, total nucleotides, and GSH and by a fairly severe deficiency of ribosephosphate pyrophosphokinase (EC 2.7.6.1.).
evidence.explanation: The original characterisation, with stippling named first among the defining features.

steps/9.description: Coarse basophilic stippling: dense blue granules of aggregated ribosomal RNA scattered through the erythrocyte on a stained film. Bound to the general erythrocyte-inclusion term because HPO has no term for basophilic stippling itself; see notes.

evidence.snippet: The nucleotidase activity in deficient red cells assayed less than 14%, and usually less than 10%, of normal and much less in terms of reticulocyte-rich blood, where it was consistently found to be increased.
evidence.explanation: Supports the assay-confounder claim through the observation that the enzyme is increased in reticulocyte-rich blood. The quote is indirect for the presence of reticulocytosis itself, which is why directness is recorded as INDIRECT.

steps/10.description: Marrow compensation for the shortened red cell lifespan. It is also an assay confounder: the enzyme is normally enriched in reticulocytes, so a reticulocytosis raises the expected activity that the measured value must be read against.

evidence.snippet: Hemolytic anemia can shorten erythrocyte lifespan, leading to varying clinical presentations depending on whether hemolysis occurs intravascularly or extravascularly.
evidence.explanation: Supports the hemolytic origin of the bilirubin load rather than naming hyperbilirubinemia directly, so directness is recorded as INDIRECT.

steps/11.description: The bilirubin load from chronic hemolysis, presenting as scleral icterus and jaundice. Co-inherited UGT1A1 Gilbert alleles were found in both reported Chinese cases and would be expected to worsen it.

evidence.snippet: Only residual activity of pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase in the brothers' erythrocytes could be observed when compared with the controls, including their asymptomatic father and sister.
evidence.explanation: Ties a specific NT5C3A genotype to the loss of enzyme activity in the patients' own red cells, with unaffected relatives as the comparison.

evidence.snippet: The pyrimidine 5'-ribonucleotides are presumably derived from RNA degradation and, not being diffusible, accumulate when the enzyme catalyzing their dephosphorylation is deficient.
evidence.explanation: States the causal step this edge asserts, and the reason the substrate cannot simply leave the cell instead.

evidence.snippet: Lead intoxication is accompanied by an acquired deficiency of erythrocyte pryimidine-specific, 5'-nucleotidase.
evidence.explanation: States that lead acts by producing a deficiency of this specific enzyme. Quoted verbatim including the source's misspelling of pyrimidine.

edges/10.description: Lead phenocopies the disease at exactly this node, inhibiting the same enzyme rather than acting anywhere else in the chain.

evidence.snippet: The DNA analysis was complicated by P5'N-1 pseudogenes found on chromosomes 4 and 7.
evidence.explanation: The pseudogene problem, from the study that first sequenced the gene.

evidence.snippet: Altogether, our results may substantiate the hypothesis of the heterogeneity of the molecular basis of the defect involving both the mutation presented here and negative regulation of expression of the "normal" allele.
evidence.explanation: The authors' proposal that a heterozygous coding genotype can still give the full phenotype through allele-specific expression.

evidence.snippet: The enzyme pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase (NT5C3A), which mediates nucleotide catabolism, was previously thought to be restricted to blood cells.
evidence.explanation: Recorded as NO_EVIDENCE deliberately. The paper establishes a real non-erythroid function for the gene, but says nothing about the hemolytic disease, and no immunological phenotype has been reported in patients. It is cited so that a reader who finds this literature is not left to infer a disease claim from it.

genes/0.notes:
Encodes cytosolic 5-nucleotidase III-A (cN-IIIA, P5N-1), on chromosome 7. Formerly written P5'N-1 or UMPH1 in the older literature.
Two practical points about sequencing this gene. P5N pseudogenes on chromosomes 4 and 7 complicated the original mutation analysis and are still a source of mapping artefact. And at least one reported family shows a genotype that does not read as straightforwardly biallelic: two brothers carried a heterozygous in-frame deletion yet expressed only the mutant transcript, so the authors proposed negative regulation of the normal allele rather than a second coding variant. A heterozygous NT5C3A finding in a patient with the biochemical phenotype should therefore not be dismissed without transcript-level work.
NT5C3A also has a function outside the red cell that is not part of this disease: it is interferon-inducible in many cell types and represses NF-kB driven cytokine transcription. No immunological phenotype has been reported in P5N-deficient patients, and this entry makes no claim that one exists.

evidence.snippet: Investigation of the promoter polymorphism of the uridine diphospho glucuronosyl transferase 1A (UGT1A) gene revealed that the father was homozygous for the allele (TA7) and the daughter heterozygous (TA6/TA7).
evidence.explanation: The UGT1A1 genotypes in a family where the paper's own title states that Gilbert syndrome influences clinical expression.

genes/1.notes:
Co-inherited Gilbert-type UGT1A1 alleles do not cause the hemolysis but change how it presents. UGT1A1 conjugates bilirubin; a reduced-activity allele on top of a chronic hemolytic load raises unconjugated bilirubin further, deepening the jaundice and, plausibly, the gallstone risk. In the father-and-daughter pair below the father was homozygous and the daughter heterozygous for the TA7 promoter allele, and the reporting paper's own title states that Gilbert syndrome influences clinical expression here. This is a modifier of clinical expression, not of the enzymopathy.
A second, independent series reports the same co-inheritance - both patients carrying UGT1A1 c.211G>A (p.G71R) - and concludes that establishing the UGT1A1 genotype is necessary to read the NT5C3A genotype-phenotype relationship accurately. That report (PMID:34547876) is not cited with an evidence item, for a tooling reason recorded in this entry's notes rather than because the finding is in doubt.

evidence.snippet: An individual homozygous for both these conditions has a severe hemolytic anemia, whereas family members who are homozygous for Hb E are asymptomatic and those homozygous for pyrimidine 5' nucleotidase deficiency have the mild hemolytic anemia that is characteristic of this disorder.
evidence.explanation: The genotype-by-genotype breakdown that establishes the interaction as more than additive.

evidence.snippet: A P5N-I gene mutation (IVS8 + 1-2delGT) was found in the family, confirming that the severe phenotype results from the interaction between two genetic diseases.
evidence.explanation: The molecular follow-up that confirms the severe phenotype is the product of two genetic lesions rather than of an unusually severe single one.

genes/2.notes: Co-inheritance of hemoglobin E converts this from a mild disorder into a severe one, and the direction of the interaction is the informative part: it is not additive. In the reported Bangladeshi family, individuals homozygous for Hb E alone were asymptomatic and those homozygous for the enzyme deficiency alone had the usual mild anemia, while the doubly homozygous individual had severe hemolytic anemia. Globin-chain work traced this to marked instability of Hb E specifically in enzyme-deficient red cells, with free alpha-chains accumulating on the membrane. This is the observation behind the oxidative-vulnerability candidate recorded on the hemolysis node.

evidence.snippet: This case underscores the necessity for genetic counseling for affected individuals and their families, as well as the importance of continued follow-up and supportive care in managing hemolytic anemia related to enzyme deficiencies.
evidence.explanation: Names supportive care and follow-up as the management, which is the absence of a disease-modifying option stated positively.

treatments/0.description: There is no treatment for the enzyme defect. Management is folate support, monitoring of the hemolysis, and transfusion during severe crises. Because both reported Chinese patients carried Gilbert-type UGT1A1 alleles and one had already developed gallstones, biliary surveillance is part of routine care.

evidence.snippet: We report a case of a 65-year-old female patient with systemic lupus erythematosus and a history of splenectomy, who was admitted for evaluation of persistent hemolytic crises.
evidence.explanation: Records both that splenectomy was performed and that hemolysis persisted after it. It does not support efficacy.

evidence.snippet: We report a rare case of haemolytic anaemia where splenectomy was carried out following trauma to a massively enlarged spleen and was followed by extreme sustained thrombocytosis associated with extensive portal, splenic and mesenteric vein thrombosis despite standard antithrombotic prophylaxis.
evidence.explanation: A severe thrombotic complication of splenectomy in this disease. Graded REFUTE against splenectomy as a management option, since it is evidence of harm rather than of absent benefit.

evidence.snippet: Reactive and redistributional thrombocytosis is a well-known postsplenectomy occurrence .Usually it is transient and it rarely reaches extreme levels.
evidence.explanation: The background that makes the reported case unusual rather than expected. Quoted verbatim including the source's own spacing error.

treatments/1.description:
Reported in patients with this disease, not established as effective, and with a documented harm. The 65-year-old case had undergone splenectomy and was nonetheless admitted for persistent hemolytic crises, so the entry records splenectomy as something that is done rather than something that works.
The harm is worth stating alongside the absent benefit. In one reported patient, splenectomy was followed by extreme sustained thrombocytosis and extensive portal, splenic and mesenteric vein thrombosis, despite standard antithrombotic prophylaxis. Post-splenectomy thrombocytosis is common and usually transient; this was neither. On the evidence in this entry the procedure has no demonstrated benefit in this disease and one severe reported complication, which is an unfavourable balance rather than an open question.

open_questions/0.rationale:
Every step from the gene to the stippled cell is well characterised, and the last one is not. Reviews written forty years after the disease was described still call the hemolytic mechanism unclear. Two long-standing observations are unexplained and may be part of the answer: reduced glutathione is raised rather than lowered in patient cells, which is the opposite of the oxidative picture in other red cell enzymopathies, and the ribose phosphate pyrophosphokinase deficiency that dominated the earliest reports was set aside as an epiphenomenon without ever being explained.
A third observation constrains any answer: residual enzyme activity does not correlate with the degree of hemolysis. Whatever the destructive step is, it is not a simple function of how much enzyme is left, which is why this node is recorded as HYPOTHETICAL rather than merely unmeasured.

open_questions/1.rationale:
HPO carries Erythrocyte inclusion bodies (HP:0020080) with three children - Pappenheimer bodies, Heinz bodies and Howell-Jolly bodies - and no term for basophilic stippling. The entry binds the parent and carries the specific concept in preferred_term. Pappenheimer bodies (HP:0020081) must not be used instead: its HPO definition happens to contain the words "basophilic stippling", but Pappenheimer bodies are iron-containing siderotic granules, a different entity with a different cause, so that term is an inviting wrong answer rather than a usable approximation. An HPO term request would let this and lead poisoning both bind the finding precisely.
The gap is not theoretical. The OpenScientist deep-research report for this disease offered HP:0011273 as "basophilic stippling of erythrocytes"; HPO calls that term Anisocytosis, defined as abnormally increased variability in erythrocyte size. The report's own term-validation section caught it. A missing term does not stay missing: something plausible gets bound in its place.

evidence.snippet: Mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III, Sanfilippo syndrome) is a lysosomal storage disorder, caused by a deficiency in one of the four enzymes involved in the catabolism of glycosaminoglycan heparan sulfate.
evidence.explanation: This review supports a shared root mechanism upstream of the four Sanfilippo subtypes: failure of lysosomal heparan sulfate catabolism.

evidence.snippet: The diagnosis of MPS III is established in a proband with suggestive clinical and laboratory findings in whom either biallelic pathogenic variants in one of four genes (GNS, HGSNAT, NAGLU, and SGSH) or deficiency of the respective lysosomal enzyme has been identified.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews confirms that the shared root disorder is genetically split across four subtype-defining lysosomal enzyme genes.

steps/0.description: The root disease mechanism is deficiency of one of four lysosomal enzymes required for the stepwise degradation of heparan sulfate.

evidence.snippet: Enzyme deficiency results in accumulation of partially degraded HS within lysosomes throughout the body, leading to a progressive severe neurological disease.
evidence.explanation: This preclinical abstract directly supports lysosomal heparan sulfate storage as the immediate consequence of enzyme deficiency.

steps/1.description: Partially degraded heparan sulfate accumulates within lysosomes and becomes the biochemical lesion that drives downstream brain pathology.

evidence.snippet: Systemic manifestations can include musculoskeletal problems (joint stiffness, contractures, scoliosis, and hip dysplasia), hearing loss, respiratory tract and sinopulmonary infections, and cardiac disease (valvular thickening, defects in the cardiac conduction system).
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews supports this as the systemic clinical branch of MPS III.

steps/2.description: Although neurologic decline dominates Sanfilippo syndrome, extraneural glycosaminoglycan storage produces a milder systemic branch involving musculoskeletal, auditory, respiratory, and cardiac manifestations.

evidence.snippet: Quantitative immunohistochemistry showed significantly increased lysosomal compartment, GM2 ganglioside storage, neuroinflammation, decreased and mislocalised synaptic vesicle associated membrane protein, (VAMP2), and decreased post-synaptic protein, Homer-1, in layers II/III-VI of the primary motor, somatosensory and parietal cortex.
evidence.explanation: IIIA and IIIB mouse models both show explicit neuroinflammatory brain pathology alongside lysosomal storage.

steps/3.description: Brain heparan sulfate storage is accompanied by microglial, astrocytic, and cytokine evidence of neuroinflammation.

evidence.snippet: Quantitative immunohistochemistry showed significantly increased lysosomal compartment, GM2 ganglioside storage, neuroinflammation, decreased and mislocalised synaptic vesicle associated membrane protein, (VAMP2), and decreased post-synaptic protein, Homer-1, in layers II/III-VI of the primary motor, somatosensory and parietal cortex.
evidence.explanation: IIIA and IIIB mouse models both show cortical synaptic protein abnormalities consistent with neuronal dysfunction.

steps/4.description: Sanfilippo syndrome includes early cortical synaptic dysfunction with abnormal synaptic vesicle and postsynaptic protein handling before overt neuronal loss becomes dominant.

evidence.snippet: Mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III) is a multisystem lysosomal storage disease characterized by progressive central nervous system degeneration manifest as severe intellectual disability (ID), developmental regression, and other neurologic manifestations including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), behavioral problems, and sleep disturbances.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews directly supports progressive CNS degeneration as the dominant disease-level consequence of Sanfilippo syndrome.

steps/5.description: The shared clinical trajectory across Sanfilippo syndrome is progressive central nervous system degeneration with worsening cognition, regression, and later premature death.

evidence.snippet: Mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III) is a multisystem lysosomal storage disease characterized by progressive central nervous system degeneration manifest as severe intellectual disability (ID), developmental regression, and other neurologic manifestations including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), behavioral problems, and sleep disturbances.

steps/3.description:
Replication-dependent histone mRNAs are not degraded on schedule, so histone supply is uncoupled from the cell cycle.
This arm is curated as its own node rather than folded into the rRNA one because the entry's tissue-restriction knowledge gap proposes chondrocyte histone supply as one candidate explanation, and a hypothesis needs a node to attach to. Both arms are housekeeping functions present in every dividing cell, which is what makes the skeletal restriction of the phenotype the open question rather than an incidental detail.

genes/0.notes: The genotype requirement is the diagnosis. At least one missense allele is needed for the skeletal disease; biallelic nulls give a different, milder phenotype. Because the missense alleles abolish catalytic activity while leaving protein behind, and are more damaging than absence of the protein, the implied mechanism is dominant-negative or neomorphic rather than simple loss of function. The entry states that as the implication the authors draw, not as a demonstrated mechanism - no experiment cited here distinguishes a dominant-negative from a neomorphic effect.

open_questions/0.rationale:
The inversion is the central finding of this disease and it is unexplained. A dominant-negative effect on a complex, a neomorphic RNA-binding activity retained by the dead enzyme, and sequestration of a substrate or partner are all consistent with what is reported, and nothing cited here distinguishes them.
This is not an academic gap. It determines what a therapy would have to do: degrading the mutant protein would help under a dominant-negative or neomorphic model and would be actively harmful under none of them, whereas restoring exoribonuclease activity would be the target under a loss-of-function model that the genetics already argues against. It also explains why the existing knockout mouse cannot serve as a preclinical model.

open_questions/1.rationale: The pathograph in this entry passes from two housekeeping RNA functions to a cartilage-specific outcome in a single step, and the patient iPSC chondrogenesis result is what licenses that step empirically without explaining it. Ribosomopathies as a class raise the same question, and the candidate answers - a proliferation-rate dependency in the growth plate, a particular sensitivity of skeletal-patterning transcripts, or a chondrocyte-specific requirement for histone supply - are not distinguished by anything cited here.

evidence.explanation: An important qualification: the block is partial, not absolute. Mutant fibronectin does reach plasma and medium, just at much lower abundance than wild type — so the extracellular pool is reduced and contaminated with mutant protein rather than simply halved. Graded IN_VITRO although the sentence spans patient plasma as well as fibroblast medium: the evidence is a mass-spectrometry assay run on patient-derived samples outside the organism, which is what IN_VITRO denotes here, not a clinical observation.

steps/2.description: The mutant fibronectin accumulates inside the cell instead of reaching the extracellular space. Immunofluorescence shows increased intracellular retention of the mutant proteins. This is the reason the disorder is best understood as a secretion defect rather than as a defect in the matrix-binding properties of fibronectin itself.

evidence.snippet: The accumulation of intracellular FN and ER proteins elevated cellular stress markers and altered mitochondrial structure.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the retained protein imposes a measurable cellular stress burden rather than being silently sequestered.

steps/3.description: Undegraded fibronectin-and-chaperone vesicles build up in the cytosol of patient-derived mesenchymal stem cells, a subset acquiring lysosomal markers. Cellular stress markers rise and mitochondrial structure is altered, and bulk RNA sequencing shows a transcriptomic profile specific to the patient cells. This is the second arm of the mechanism, distinct from simple extracellular deficiency: the mutant protein does harm inside the cell as well as failing to act outside it, which is the strongest argument yet that the disorder is not plain haploinsufficiency.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, FN mutant cells exhibited significantly lower transforming growth factor beta-1 (TGFβ1) expression, crucial for mesenchymal condensation.
evidence.explanation: Identifies reduced TGF-beta-1 as the signalling deficit behind the condensation failure; the same sentence notes TGF-beta-1 is crucial for mesenchymal condensation.

evidence.snippet: Exogenous FN or TGFβ1 supplementation effectively improved the MSC condensation and promoted chondrogenesis in FN mutant cells.
evidence.explanation: The rescue experiment, and the first point of pharmacological leverage identified in this disorder: the condensation defect is reversible in vitro by supplying either the missing matrix protein or the growth factor downstream of it.

steps/4.description: Mesenchymal condensation is the first committed step of skeletogenesis, and it fails in FN1-mutant cells. The proximate reason appears to be a shortfall of TGF-beta-1, which mutant cells express at significantly lower levels and which condensation requires. The finding is reversible in vitro: supplying either exogenous fibronectin or TGF-beta-1 restores condensation and promotes chondrogenesis, which makes this the first identified point of pharmacological leverage in the disorder.

evidence.snippet: It is also known to play roles in skeletal tissues through its secretion by osteoblasts, chondrocytes, and mesenchymal cells.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the skeletal cell types that secrete fibronectin and therefore the tissue in which the defect acts.

steps/5.description: Fibronectin is secreted in skeletal tissue by osteoblasts, chondrocytes, and mesenchymal cells, so a secretion defect acts locally in exactly the compartments where the disease manifests. The failure is of matrix assembly at sites of active endochondral growth.

evidence.snippet: The most striking feature characterizing SMD-CF is irregularly shaped metaphyses giving the appearance of "corner fractures".
evidence.explanation: Defines the primary radiographic lesion.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, the distal femoral changes in this patient healed with skeletal maturation.
evidence.explanation: Documents that the metaphyseal lesion is not necessarily permanent, which matters for the natural history.

steps/6.description: Irregularly shaped metaphyses carrying flake-like, triangular, or curvilinear ossification centres at their edges. The appearance simulates a healing corner fracture, which is the source of the disorder's name and of its main diagnostic hazard: a child with these radiographs has repeatedly been investigated for non-accidental injury. The changes involve the distal tibia, the ulnar aspect of the distal radius, and the proximal humerus and femur, and in at least one patient the distal femoral changes healed with skeletal maturation.

evidence.snippet: The severe scoliosis in most individuals and rare developmental coxa vara distinguish individuals with FN1 mutations from those with classical Sutcliffe-type SMD.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the FN1 subtype is clinically separable from the classical radiographic entity.

steps/7.description: Ovoid vertebral bodies with severe scoliosis and developmental coxa vara. Severe scoliosis in most individuals, together with the rare coxa vara, is what separates the FN1 cases from classical Sutcliffe-type SMD.

evidence.snippet: In addition, generalized skeletal fragility with low-trauma bilateral femoral fractures was identified in one patient.
evidence.explanation: A single-patient observation, which is why the node is curated as provisional rather than as an established feature.

evidence.snippet: We report a case of a female individual with severe spine osteoporosis diagnosed at age 52.
evidence.explanation: An independent adult observation of severe spinal osteoporosis, which upgrades reduced bone strength from a single paediatric fragility observation to a feature seen at both ends of life.

steps/8.description: Generalised skeletal fragility with low-trauma bilateral femoral fractures was identified in one of five patients in the expansion series. Whether reduced bone strength is a genuine part of the FN1 phenotype or an isolated observation is not resolved, and the distinction matters clinically because a fragility fracture on top of pseudo-fracture radiographs compounds the risk of a mistaken child protection referral.

evidence.snippet: Vision impairment and glaucoma have been reported.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the ocular arm of the extraskeletal phenotype as reported rather than theoretical.

steps/9.description: Raised intraocular pressure and hypertension, both carrying explicit annual surveillance recommendations in FN1-related disease. Neither has a worked-out mechanism here. Note that FN1 also causes glomerulopathy with fibronectin deposits through a different allelic series, which makes a renal contribution to the hypertension worth considering rather than assuming — this entry does not curate that disorder.

evidence.snippet: The most striking feature characterizing SMD-CF is irregularly shaped metaphyses giving the appearance of "corner fractures".
evidence.explanation: The feature is definitional: the cohort was assembled by this radiographic appearance, which is why the frequency is OBLIGATE.

steps/10.description: Flake-like, triangular, or curvilinear ossification centres at the margins of irregular metaphyses, simulating healing fractures. This is the defining and ascertaining feature of the entity.

evidence.snippet: The severe scoliosis in most individuals and rare developmental coxa vara distinguish individuals with FN1 mutations from those with classical Sutcliffe-type SMD.
evidence.explanation: "Most individuals" supports the VERY_FREQUENT band and the SEVERE severity qualifier.

steps/11.description: Severe scoliosis is present in most individuals with FN1 variants and is one of the two features separating them from classical Sutcliffe-type SMD.

evidence.snippet: An array of secondary features, including developmental coxa vara, ovoid vertebral bodies and severe scoliosis, may also be present.
evidence.explanation: Lists coxa vara among the secondary features that may be present, supporting an OCCASIONAL band.

steps/12.description: Reduction of the femoral neck-shaft angle developing after birth. Explicitly described as rare within the FN1 group, but its presence still points away from classical Sutcliffe-type SMD.

evidence.snippet: An array of secondary features, including developmental coxa vara, ovoid vertebral bodies and severe scoliosis, may also be present.
evidence.explanation: Names ovoid vertebral bodies among the secondary features.

steps/13.description: Egg-shaped vertebral bodies, the vertebral component that makes this a spondylometaphyseal rather than a purely metaphyseal dysplasia.

evidence.snippet: Our child had short stature, facial dysmorphism, spondylometaphyseal dysplasia and corner fractures
evidence.explanation: Documents short stature in a molecularly confirmed FN1 patient.

steps/14.description: Short stature, with growth-plate irregularities and vertebral anomalies, is part of the general presentation of the spondylometaphyseal dysplasias and was present in the reported FN1 cases.

evidence.snippet: In addition, generalized skeletal fragility with low-trauma bilateral femoral fractures was identified in one patient.
evidence.explanation: One patient in five supports an OCCASIONAL band.

steps/15.description: Generalised skeletal fragility with low-trauma bilateral femoral fractures in one of five patients in the expansion series. Distinct from the pseudo-fractures that name the disorder — these were real fractures.

evidence.snippet: Images showed spinal cord compression and injury associated with os odontoideum and C1-C2 instability.
evidence.explanation: Documents the odontoid anomaly and the instability, together with the cord injury they caused.

evidence.snippet: This paper describes the first case of SMD-CF FN1-related accompanied by odontoid anomalies.
evidence.explanation: A first report, which is why the frequency band is OCCASIONAL and the entry does not claim it as an established feature.

steps/16.description: An odontoid anomaly with C1-C2 instability, reported once in a girl who presented at 11.9 years with acute quadriparesis from spinal cord compression and injury. She required decompression and instrumented occipitocervical stabilisation and was left with residual paraparesis. Odontoid abnormalities were not part of the recognised vertebral spectrum before this report.

evidence.snippet: Little has been reported regarding the natural history of SMDCF: our patient presented to the adult endocrine clinic with early postmenopausal osteoporosis.
evidence.explanation: Documents the osteoporosis and states directly that the adult natural history is otherwise unreported.

steps/17.description: Severe spinal osteoporosis diagnosed at age 52 in a woman carrying a childhood diagnosis of SMDCF, who presented to an adult endocrine clinic with early postmenopausal osteoporosis. The adult natural history of this disorder is barely documented, so whether this is a disease feature or a coincidence of menopause is not settled — but it sits alongside the paediatric fragility fractures reported separately.

evidence.snippet: Her scoliosis was mild, and she admitted to continued limb pain that had been present since childhood.
evidence.explanation: Documents chronic limb pain persisting into adulthood despite mild radiographic deformity.

steps/18.description: Limb pain continuing from childhood into adulthood, reported in the adult index case alongside only mild scoliosis. A reminder that the symptom burden of this disorder is not fully captured by its radiographic severity.

evidence.snippet: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, corner fracture type (SMDCF) is a skeletal dysplasia characterized by short stature and a waddling gait in early childhood.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews names the waddling gait alongside short stature as the presenting picture.

steps/19.description: Waddling gait in early childhood, following from the coxa vara, and often the first thing a parent notices.

evidence.snippet: Limited joint mobility and chronic pain are common.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews records limited joint mobility as common, and in the same sentence corroborates the chronic limb pain recorded separately here.

steps/20.description: Limited joint mobility, described as common and a substantial contributor to functional burden alongside the chronic pain.

evidence.snippet: Contact sports if atlantoaxial instability is present; activities that cause joint strain in those with joint pain.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews lists atlantoaxial instability among the complications requiring activity restriction, which establishes it as a recognised feature.

steps/21.description: Atlantoaxial instability occurs and requires surgical assessment; its presence contraindicates contact sports. No frequency band is set because the source states that it occurs and must be managed, not how often. It is the same cervical vulnerability the single reported os odontoideum case made concrete — two independent sources converging on the craniocervical junction as the site of greatest risk in this disorder.

evidence.snippet: Vision impairment and glaucoma have been reported.
evidence.explanation: GeneReviews records glaucoma among the manifestations.

steps/22.description: Vision impairment and glaucoma have been reported, and annual intraocular pressure measurement is recommended specifically in FN1-related disease. This is the extra-skeletal feature most likely to be missed in a patient followed by orthopaedics alone.

evidence.snippet: Annual evaluation of intraocular pressure and blood pressure in individuals with FN1-related SMDCF.
evidence.explanation: The surveillance recommendation establishes both hypertension and raised intraocular pressure as recognised concerns specific to this subtype.

steps/23.description: Hypertension requires management in some patients, and annual blood-pressure measurement is recommended in FN1-related disease. Worth noting that FN1 variants also cause glomerulopathy with fibronectin deposits — a different allelic series — which makes a renal contribution worth considering rather than assuming.

evidence.snippet: The wild-type rF70K and rFN were secreted into the culture medium, whereas all mutant proteins were either not secreted or secreted at significantly lower amounts.
evidence.explanation: A direct functional demonstration that the variants act by blocking secretion.

edges/1.description: Recombinant expression of the disease alleles, in both the secreted N-terminal 70 kDa fragment and full-length fibronectin, shows that the mutant proteins are not secreted or are secreted at significantly reduced levels, and are retained inside the cell.

evidence.snippet: FN and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein folding chaperones (BIP, HSP47) accumulated in MSCs within ribosome-covered cytosolic vesicles that emerged from the ER.
evidence.explanation: Identifies the subcellular fate of the retained protein in the cell type where the disorder acts.

edges/2.description: The retained protein is not inert. In patient-derived mesenchymal stem cells it accumulates with the endoplasmic reticulum chaperones BIP and HSP47 inside ribosome-covered cytosolic vesicles budding from the ER, most of which are never cleared.

evidence.snippet: Analyses of plasma samples from SMDCF patients also showed reduced FN in circulation.
evidence.explanation: Confirms in patients that the secretion defect measured in vitro produces a real extracellular deficit.

evidence.snippet: Immunofluorescence and immunoblotting analyses show that mutant fibroblasts assemble significantly lower amounts of FN matrix than wild-type cells
evidence.explanation: The direct measurement of the step this edge asserts. Everything else on this edge measures fibronectin levels — in plasma, in medium — whereas this measures assembled matrix, which is the quantity the disorder is about.

evidence.snippet: Fibronectin is a master organizer of extracellular matrices (ECMs) and promotes the assembly of collagens, fibrillin-1, and other proteins.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the organising role whose loss makes a secretion defect a matrix-assembly defect.

edges/3.description: Fibronectin that never reaches the extracellular space cannot nucleate matrix assembly. Because fibronectin organises the deposition of collagens and fibrillin-1, the consequence is not the loss of one matrix component but a failure of the assembly step on which several depend. The extracellular deficit is systemic as well as local: circulating fibronectin is reduced in patient plasma.

evidence.snippet: Analysis of MSC differentiation into chondrocytes showed impaired mesenchymal condensation, reduced chondrogenic markers, and compromised cell proliferation in mutant cells.
evidence.explanation: The cellular endpoint that connects the secretion defect to a growth-plate phenotype, measured in a patient-derived system.

edges/4.description: Mutant mesenchymal stem cells condense poorly, express fewer chondrogenic markers, and proliferate less on differentiation to chondrocytes.

edges/5.description: Failure of condensation and chondrogenesis at the growth plate is the cellular route from the secretion defect to the metaphyseal lesion. The intervening growth-plate steps are not directly observed in this system, which uses patient-derived cells rather than growth-plate tissue.

evidence.snippet: The abnormal metaphyseal ossification and "corner fracture" appearances were the most remarkable clinical feature in these patients.
evidence.explanation: Names abnormal metaphyseal ossification as the dominant clinical-radiographic finding.

edges/6.description: Disordered matrix assembly at the growth plate produces irregular metaphyseal ossification, the primary radiographic lesion.

evidence.snippet: Annual evaluation of intraocular pressure and blood pressure in individuals with FN1-related SMDCF.
evidence.explanation: A surveillance recommendation is evidence that these are recognised consequences of the genotype, not evidence of the route by which they arise.

edges/7.description: Fibronectin is a systemic matrix protein, not a skeletal one, and circulating levels are reduced in patients — so extraskeletal consequences are expected in principle. GeneReviews recommends annual intraocular-pressure and blood-pressure surveillance in FN1-related disease specifically, which is a clinical recognition of that expectation. No mechanism has been worked out for either, which is why the edge carries unknown intermediates.

evidence.snippet: emphasizes the importance of FN in bone formation and possibly also in the maintenance of bone strength
evidence.explanation: The authors' own hedged phrasing — "possibly also" — is why this edge is graded INDIRECT with unknown intermediates.

edges/8.description: A single reported patient had generalised skeletal fragility with low-trauma bilateral femoral fractures, which the authors take as a signal that fibronectin may also maintain bone strength. This is one observation in one patient and is curated as a hypothesis, not an established feature.

edges/9.description: The flake-like, triangular, or curvilinear marginal ossification centres that name the disorder are the direct radiographic read-out of this node.

edges/10.description: Disordered ossification across the growth plates reduces stature, one of the general features of the spondylometaphyseal dysplasias.

evidence.snippet: An array of secondary features, including developmental coxa vara, ovoid vertebral bodies and severe scoliosis, may also be present.
evidence.explanation: Names the three secondary skeletal features.

edges/11.description: Alongside the metaphyseal lesion, ovoid vertebral bodies, developmental coxa vara, and severe scoliosis make up the secondary skeletal phenotype.

edges/12.description: The vertebral body shape abnormality of the dysplasia.

edges/13.description: Severe scoliosis in most individuals with FN1 variants, one of the two features separating them from classical Sutcliffe-type SMD.

edges/14.description: Postnatal reduction of the femoral neck-shaft angle, rare within the FN1 group but pointing away from the classical entity when present.

edges/15.description: The coxa vara and the limb malalignment together produce the waddling gait that is often the presenting sign in early childhood.

edges/16.description: Progressive deformity restricts joint range, described as common and a major contributor to functional burden.

edges/17.description: The vertebral dysplasia extends to the craniocervical junction, where it manifests as atlantoaxial instability requiring surgical assessment.

evidence.snippet: Vertebral changes as delayed vertebral ossification, ovoid vertebral bodies, anterior vertebral wedging, and platyspondyly have been observed in this condition, while odontoid abnormalities have not been reported.
evidence.explanation: States both the established vertebral spectrum and that the odontoid anomaly falls outside it, which is why the edge is hedged.

edges/18.description: Odontoid anomaly has been reported once, in a girl who presented at 11.9 years with acute quadriparesis from cord compression. Vertebral change is established in this disorder and the odontoid is a vertebral ossification centre, but the report is explicit that odontoid abnormalities had not previously been described here, so a single case cannot establish the link as a regular consequence.

edges/19.description: Generalised skeletal fragility with low-trauma bilateral femoral fractures in one reported child. Distinct from the pseudo-fractures that name the disorder.

edges/20.description: Severe spinal osteoporosis diagnosed at 52 in a woman with a childhood SMDCF diagnosis, presenting to an adult endocrine clinic.

edges/21.description: Limb pain persisting from childhood into the sixth decade. Whether it tracks bone strength, the metaphyseal lesion, or the deformity is not established.

edges/22.description: Raised intraocular pressure with reported glaucoma; the trabecular meshwork is a fibronectin-rich outflow structure, which is a plausible but untested route.

edges/23.description: Hypertension requiring management in some patients, with no established mechanism in this disorder.

evidence.snippet: By comparing the exomes of individuals with SMD with the radiographic appearance of "corner fractures" at metaphyses, we identified three individuals with fibronectin (FN1) variants affecting highly conserved residues.
evidence.explanation: The gene-discovery result, from a radiographically defined cohort.

evidence.snippet: All individuals shared a substitution of a cysteine residue, disrupting disulfide bonds in the FN type-I assembly domains located in the N-terminal assembly region.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the cysteine-substitution, disulfide-disrupting pattern that unifies the allelic spectrum and localises it to the assembly region.

evidence.snippet: Standard treatment for scoliosis per orthopedist; surgical treatment for coxa vara, genu valgum or varum, bowing of the tibia, leg length discrepancy, atlantoaxial instability per orthopedist
evidence.explanation: The GeneReviews management recommendation, which names the specific deformities requiring orthopaedic referral in this disorder. Expert consensus rather than study evidence, hence OTHER.

treatments/0.description: Care is orthopaedic and supportive: monitoring and surgical management of severe scoliosis, of developmental coxa vara, and of progressive limb malalignment. No disease-modifying therapy exists and no management study specific to FN1-related SMD-CF has been published.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, using matching tools and the SkelDys emailing list, we identified other individuals with de novo FN1 variants and a similar phenotype.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the de novo, dominant pattern that determines the recurrence-risk counselling.

treatments/1.description: An affected individual's offspring risk is 50 percent, and a multigenerational family with four affected members shows that transmission does happen. Where the proband's variant is genuinely de novo the parental recurrence risk is low but not zero because of gonadal mosaicism. Testing the parents is therefore part of counselling rather than an academic exercise — it decides which of two quite different recurrence conversations applies.

evidence.snippet: All individuals shared a substitution of a cysteine residue, disrupting disulfide bonds in the FN type-I assembly domains located in the N-terminal assembly region.
evidence.explanation: The narrowness and chemical uniformity of the allelic spectrum is the observation that makes simple haploinsufficiency an unlikely full explanation.

evidence.snippet: Massive amounts of these vesicles were not cleared from the cytosol, and a smaller subset showed the presence of lysosomal markers.
evidence.explanation: An intracellular burden of this scale is a consequence a null allele cannot produce, which is the strongest evidence against pure haploinsufficiency.

open_questions/0.rationale: Partly answered since this entry was first written, and worth stating precisely how far. A 2024 patient-derived iPSC study shows the mechanism has two arms, not one: extracellular fibronectin is reduced — in patient plasma as well as in culture — and the retained mutant protein simultaneously accumulates with ER chaperones in uncleared cytosolic vesicles, raising cellular stress markers and distorting mitochondrial structure. That intracellular arm is a gain of toxic consequence and cannot be produced by a null allele, which argues against simple haploinsufficiency; the allelic spectrum, almost uniformly cysteine substitutions in one small region, points the same way. What remains untested is the decisive comparison: no study has put a truncating and a missense FN1 allele side by side in the same cell background. Until that is done the relative contribution of the two arms is unknown, and it is exactly what decides whether therapy should aim to raise wild-type output or to clear the retained mutant. Note that the rescue result — exogenous fibronectin or TGF-beta-1 restoring condensation — works through the extracellular arm and does not settle the question.

evidence.snippet: We consider differences and similarities between MCD Brussels and SMD-FN1, by reviewing literature on both conditions and assess whether they are in fact the same disorder.
evidence.explanation: The entity question is posed explicitly in the literature.

evidence.snippet: The severe scoliosis in most individuals and rare developmental coxa vara distinguish individuals with FN1 mutations from those with classical Sutcliffe-type SMD.
evidence.explanation: The founding report already separates the FN1 cases from the classical entity on clinical grounds, which is the first evidence that the radiographic label covers more than one disorder.

open_questions/1.rationale: The entity was defined radiographically decades before any gene was known, and the label has since accumulated cases attributed to FN1 and to COL2A1 — the latter not including the original Sutcliffe family. A separate report asks outright whether metaphyseal chondrodysplasia Brussels type and FN1-related SMD are the same disorder. The ISDS nosology and MONDO both encode the unresolved state rather than settling it: the nosology lists MIM 184255 in both the SMD group and the type 2 collagen group, and MONDO gives the class two parents. Any downstream analysis that treats this concept as a single gene-defined disease will be wrong about some of its members.
